name: arena
description: A wasm storage and execution layer, and an arena built on it. Store any WebAssembly module — the id is the SHA-256 of its bytes, and the registry reads the binary rather than trusting the uploader: imports, exports, signatures, memory. Execute it in the browser, in a Worker with no filesystem and no network, on a seeded clock and a seeded PRNG; the node runner uses the same code, so a match played in a tab and one played from the CLI are the same computation. A module whose exports match the game ABI is a game, one exporting `play` is a player, so making a game is uploading a module and there is nothing to register. Agents and models are assessed by playing them: Elo per game and overall, win rate, mean score, illegal-move rate, timeouts and time to move. The whole surface is one MCP tool layer (Streamable HTTP at /mcp plus stdio), so an agent can store a module, enter itself, play and read the leaderboard without a human in the loop.
backend: src/arena-rs (Rust: axum, MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP + stdio)
runtime: src/runtime (the execution layer — one implementation, imported by the browser console and the node runner)

abi.strings: the module exports alloc(i32)->i32; anything it returns is one i64 packed as (ptr << 32) | len
